# Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime — facts

> Source-anchored units about Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime: 19 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 19 units · 3 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] find() returns a Cursor of matches; find_one() returns Result<Option<T>>, with Some for a match and None when no document matches. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] Serde rename changes the serialized and deserialized field name, and default supplies Default::default() when a field is absent during deserialization. These attributes customize Rust-to-BSON mapping in the driver. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Enable the blocking API with the sync Cargo feature and import types from mongodb::sync. The quick reference executes synchronous CRUD actions with run(), alongside async examples using await. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/runtimes.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-rust-driver, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/reference/quick-reference.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] find_one distinguishes no match from an error through Result<Option<T>>: a matching document yields Some, and no match yields None. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] Read options can be chained directly before awaiting the operation; examples use sort, limit and projection. The retrieval guide cautions that earlier driver APIs instead construct an options object and pass it to the find method. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/reference/quick-reference.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Serde rename changes a serialized and deserialized field name. The driver integrates Serde attributes into custom mapping, allowing a Rust field name to differ from its stored name. (high confidence) — https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md
- [statement] For missing fields, Serde default uses Default::default(); skip suppresses both serialization and deserialization. These differ from custom serialize_with and deserialize_with field helpers. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] The driver README snapshot warns that dropping unfinished driver futures for cancellation or timeout can leave internal state inconsistent. It recommends polling them to completion and suggests timing out a spawned task’s JoinHandle instead of the driver future directly. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-rust-driver · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] Serde skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none" omits a None field when serializing. This is a conditional serialization rule, unlike skip, which suppresses both serialization and deserialization. (low confidence) — https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Rust driver 3.0 removed async-std support; its asynchronous API requires Tokio. Guidance that offers both runtimes applies to the 2.x driver. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/runtimes.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-rust-driver/blob/main/migration-3.0.md
- [statement] In driver 3.0, options can be chained directly onto an operation before awaiting it, replacing the older separate options argument; a session can also be chained. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-rust-driver/blob/main/migration-3.0.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md
- [statement] Model stored documents with a custom Rust type deriving Serialize and Deserialize, and use that type as the Collection generic parameter. The driver serializes inserted instances through Serde. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md
- [statement] A typed collection can be cloned with another document type through clone_with_type(); the serialization guide demonstrates Square and Circle views of the same shapes collection. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] The asynchronous cursor idiom is to await find(), then repeatedly await try_next(); the quick reference also shows try_collect().await to collect results. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/reference/quick-reference.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] CRUD uses collection methods such as insert_one, update_one, replace_one, and delete_one. The asynchronous examples await the operation; filters and update expressions use BSON doc! documents, including $set for field updates. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/reference/quick-reference.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] ObjectId conversion helpers depend on the BSON major version: the serialization guide distinguishes BSON 3.0 serde_as helpers from BSON 2.x serialize_with helpers and shows object_id::FromHexString for a String _id. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] find returns a Cursor for matching documents. Async examples iterate it with try_next().await?; the full example imports futures::TryStreamExt. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/reference/quick-reference.md
- [statement] Custom field conversion can use serialize_with and deserialize_with functions, or with to select a module supplying both operations. The Rust driver documents these Serde hooks for BSON mapping. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html
- [statement] Beginning with Rust driver v3.0, Tokio is the only supported asynchronous runtime. An async-std application can host a Tokio Runtime and spawn driver work on it, using the same Runtime instance for Client creation and operations. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/runtimes.md · keywords: Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
